Jamal Murray is doing a pretty good job campaigning for his second straight All-Star nod, averaging a career-high 25.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, 5.7 assists, and 1.2 steals per game for the Denver Nuggets. He's given the team what they needed after the front office opted to run it back with the championship core, while his teammates haven't.
 Murray has been carrying the bulk of the weight, alongside Nikola Joki, who is starting to look like himself after a shaky start to the season, averaging 24.1 points per game on 51.7% shooting from the field. In November, though, the center is averaging 25.9 points on 54% shooting.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But what about the rest of the team ?
 Nuggets can't waste what Jamal Murray is giving them
 Christian Braun is the team's third-highest scorer, averaging 12.8 points per game, followed by Cam Johnson at 11.4 and Aaron Gordon at 11.2. There is no clear-cut third option behind Murray and Joki, a role that DeMar DeRozan took over in Wednesday's win over the Celtics, but he's had his share of offensive struggles this season, too.
 DeRozan can serve as a temporary fix when necessary, but the Nuggets need more from Braun, Johnson, and Gordon. Denver used to be able to rely on the latter, who evolved into an offensive weapon alongside Murray and Joki, but he's been trending downward. At 31 and coming off a couple of injury-ridden seasons, perhaps AG will never play with the same force and explosiveness again.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Maybe AG can be a little more productive than he has been, since he's shooting a career-low 42.1% from the field. But Braun and Johnson should be feeling the most pressure to turn things around and help supplement Murray's production. Specifically, Johnson, whom the Nuggets need to rely on from beyond the arc. He shot 1-for-16 from three in the past three games.
 Murray has been excellent (and not just on offense), but he can't carry the weight alone. He and Joki can't carry it alone, either. If Braun or Johnson aren't capable of playing, or at least sharing, that role, the Nuggets may have to make a move at the deadline to strengthen the roster for a hopeful playoff push.
 Jamal Murray is living up to the hype
 Not long ago, there was speculation that trading Murray was the route Denver needed to take to extend its championship window. The four-year, $208 million extension he signed before the 2024-25 season (which kicked in at the start of 2025-26) wasn't viewed favorably.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Murray responded by having the best season of his career in 2025-26, breaking the trend of slow starts. And he's back to doing the same at the start of this season, but he's playing even better. Part of that may be because he's had to take over, and if so, he's risen to the challenge.
 Denver has a +7.4 net rating with Murray on the floor, and a -19.1 net rating with him off (a +26.5-point differential).
 He's played in all 13 of the team's games, averaging 36.5 minutes per contest (Joki is averaging 35.7). It's worth wondering whether Murray can sustain that level of production for a full season (he doesn't need to play all 82 games) and carry it into the playoffs.
 Getting consistent help from teammates not named Joki would help with that, but will it happen?
